texts: My uncle spent his whole life collecting medals, land and compliments, and at the funeral his hands lay open and bare; I even saw the old hunter's arrow he kept on the wall and wondered what he took
The arrow flies to its mark with nothing in its hand, and the soul departs just so, with no coin or crown to carry
doha about how nobody takes anything with them when they die, with an arrow in it
arrow, nothing goes along
Write a Kabir-style doha where a flying arrow carries nothing but its own flight, just as every person leaves the world carrying no wealth, no kin and no fame on the final road
Dew sits on the grass at dawn like a jewelled treasure, yet it leaves with nothing, as we leave with empty hands
Please write a doha about the dew that gathers on every blade overnight and is gone by noon, taking nothing along, just as a rich man gathers wealth all his life and goes out with bare hands
dew, bare hands
doha with dew in it, about how we all leave with nothing
My father saved every rupee for forty years and I watched his hands this morning, open and empty on the hospital sheet, like the dew gone from the lawn by noon

Write a doha about the cremation ground where a rich man arrives with his family and his fame left outside, and a date palm stands beyond the wall, to show that nobody takes anything on that last journey
doha with a cremation ground and a date palm, about leaving with nothing at all
After the rites at the cremation ground, a date palm was swaying and my cousin said, he built three buildings and took none of them with him; I want a doha about that
Under a date palm at the cremation ground the rich man's coins stay behind, and only his silence goes along
cremation ground, date palm, nothing
Please write a doha in which a bell rings under the stars as a rich man leaves the world, and he takes with him neither his coins nor his kinsmen, since nothing at all can travel on that last road
The bell tolls under the stars for one who owned a hundred villages, and he departs with not so much as a handful of them
doha about a bell and the stars, and how you leave with nothing when you go
At my grandfather's funeral the bell rang and stars were out, and I thought of how he spent everything on land and left with nothing in his hands
bell, stars, leaving with nothing
Write a doha about the bier on which every person is carried, king or pauper, with no wealth, no relatives and no reputation going along with him on the final journey
I walked behind a bier yesterday carrying a man who owned half our street, and not even the keys to his shop came along
bier, nothing goes along
doha about someone on a bier, all their stuff stays behind
The bier carries what the world gave back, a body, and nothing else, no purse, no title, no beloved face
The mountain keeps its ore in the dark and the moneylender keeps his in a chest, and both stay behind when the owner goes
doha with a mountain and a moneylender, he leaves everything behind when he dies
mountain, moneylender, leaves nothing
The moneylender who lived below the mountain boasted about his savings for years, and now his sons fight over them while he lies in the earth with nothing in his fists
Please write a Kabir-style doha about a moneylender who piled up wealth as high as a mountain, and who left the world with the same bare hands with which he entered it, taking no coin and no kin
nothing goes along
Born with closed fists and dying with open palms, we pass through the world and carry out no more than we brought in
Cleaning out my late father's drawers I found only old receipts and a few letters, and it hit me that none of what he worked for came with him
doha about leaving with nothing at the end, please
Kabir tells us that wealth, relatives and a good name all stay behind when the last journey begins, so please write a doha reminding me that every person goes out of the world with nothing
house, cotton, empty hands
The house you built stands and the cotton you stored waits, but your hands go out as bare as they came
My uncle built a house with six rooms and stacked cotton in the loft for years, and when he died his sons were measuring the walls before the rites ended
Please write a doha about a man who built a great house and filled it with cotton to sell, thinking it was his, but who left it all behind and went on the final journey with bare hands
doha with a house and cotton in it, about leaving with nothing
My grandfather owned the grindstone, the fields and the land around, and a week after he died the family had divided every bit of it; he went with nothing
doha about leaving empty handed, use the grindstone in it
The grindstone grinds the grain of a lifetime into flour and the master leaves without a pinch in his fist
grindstone, nothing goes along
Write a doha in the voice of Kabir telling us that the grindstone turns for the rich and the poor alike, and when it stops, neither takes any grain or coin or relative along on the last journey
cage, parrot, nothing carried
Please write a doha about a rich man who keeps a parrot in a cage and counts his treasures, but who departs the world without the parrot, the cage, or a single coin from his hoard
The parrot in its cage will not follow the master, nor will the cage, nor the coins; the soul goes alone
After my aunt died, her parrot kept calling her name from its cage, and I thought of all the jewellery she left that no one wants; she took none of it
doha with a parrot and a cage, about how nobody takes anything when they die
The tree gives its shade to everyone, and the philosopher's stone turns metals, but the owner who clutched either leaves with open hands
tree, philosopher's stone, nothing carried
Write a doha in which a seeker finds the philosopher's stone beneath a tree and grows rich beyond measure, but dies leaving all of it behind, taking neither fortune nor fame with him on the last road
My great-uncle searched all his life for a philosopher's stone in the hills, and under a tree at the end he died with nothing in his bag; I want a doha for that
doha with a tree and a philosopher's stone, you take nothing with you in the end
doha about a bee that collects honey all summer and loses it all, like us
bee, nothing goes along
A bee has been building in our wall for years and when the hive was taken down, I thought of my father who gathered and gathered and left with nothing
The bee gathers honey for a lifetime and sips none at its last breath, and so man gathers wealth and sails out bare
Please write a Kabir-style doha where a bee works through the whole summer to store honey that someone else will take, just as a person gathers wealth that must be left behind at the final journey
The moon and the mountain keep their splendour, but the one who owned the valley leaves with empty hands under both
moon, mountain, bare departure
We buried my grandfather on a mountain slope under the moon, a man who once owned most of the valley, and the sons were already talking about papers; he took none of it
Write a doha in which the moon looks down on a mountain and a rich man's grave, and the verse says that his land, his family and his name stayed behind and only his silence went on the last road
doha with the moon and a mountain about how you leave everything behind
At my grandmother's funeral the swan on the pond didn't even look up, and my uncle, who fought over her property for ten years, stood with empty hands and wept
Write a doha about a swan that drifts across the pond carrying nothing, and compare it to a person whose long life of collecting ends with a bare journey out of this world, no kin and no coin
swan, leaves with nothing
The swan floats on the water with all its whiteness and nothing in its beak, a teacher for those who heap up wealth
doha about a swan and leaving the world with nothing, please
churn, nothing carried
My mother's churn sits in the kitchen but she is gone; she gave and saved all her life and took nothing with her but a single bangle
The churn gives butter to the household, and the churner leaves without even the foam on her hands
Please write a doha about the churn that makes butter for the family all day long, to show that the one who works and hoards must also leave the world without even a spoonful of his earnings
doha with a churn about how nobody takes anything with them
Write a doha in which a man warms his hands at a fire and counts his pearl, yet at the end of the night the fire dies and the pearl stays behind, as everything stays behind when the soul departs
My father admired his one pearl every evening by the fire and boasted, but at the end, the pearl was left in a tin box and the fire went cold; he took none of it
The fire gives up its glow and the pearl its shine, and the man goes out to the dark, with neither
fire, pearl, nothing carried
doha with a fire and a pearl, you take nothing at the end
Write a doha about a closed door and a cloth sheet spread over a body, showing that neither the wealth in the room nor the relatives crying at the door could go with him on the last journey
Behind the door and the cloth sheet, a rich man lies and his coins and kin stay outside, none able to cross
When my uncle died we shut the door and put a cloth sheet over him, and I thought of his three vehicles in the yard; none of them could follow him
doha with a door and a cloth sheet, no one takes anything on that journey
door, cloth sheet, nothing carried
doha with a fire in it, everything stays behind when you die
Write a doha about a flickering fire that burns up a lifetime of effort and wealth, leaving only the plain truth that no one carries wealth, kin or fame on that final journey
My neighbour spent his life stacking up money, and when the fire at the rites burned low, his sons argued about the will in the courtyard while he lay with empty hands
The fire eats the robe, the title and the pride, and what leaves with the rising smoke is only a breath
fire, empty hands
Kabir would say that kings and beggars alike go from the world carrying nothing, no treasure, no brothers, no title, so please write a doha that says this plainly and does not decorate it
Three brothers argued all week over the property of their father, who is still warm in the ground; he took none of it with him
Open the fist at the last hour, for what was gripped so tightly was only borrowed
doha about nothing going with you when you die, no wealth no family
empty hands
Please write a doha about a person who gathered land, cattle, a big family and a respected name, and who at the end walked the last road alone, with nothing in his hands and none of them beside him
doha about how you cant take anything with you
My neighbour was the richest man in the district, and at his funeral half the town came to look at the car park; he was carried out with not a coin
nothing goes along
Rich or poor, the road at the end admits only the walker, never his luggage
My grandfather chased a philosopher's stone and wealth all his life, and at the end I saw him lying with open hands, taking none of it
doha with a philosopher's stone, you leave with nothing anyway
philosopher's stone, bare hands
Even the philosopher's stone cannot turn a life into something the soul may carry across
Write a doha about a man who finally finds the philosopher's stone and is able to make unlimited wealth, but dies with it all behind him, empty-handed like the poorest man on the last journey
I helped clean my aunt's cupboard after she passed, sarees and jewellery all folded neatly, and she left the world in a plain wrap with nothing else
nothing goes along
doha on how you leave with nothing, no matter how much you own
The purse is full, the heart is full, and the last journey asks for neither
Write a doha reminding the reader that fame, kin and fortune stay behind at the moment of death, that no one has ever carried them across, and that the wise therefore hold them lightly
Every guest at the wedding of the world leaves without the gifts, and the host leaves without his dwelling
My cousin's father left behind two shops, a farm and a big family, and at the funeral we realised he took not one thing; the farm is already being divided
doha about how nothing goes along with us when we go
bare departure
Please write a doha in the voice of Kabir that says nothing of the world's wealth, family or name accompanies a person on the last road, and that the true account is only of what he has done
doha with a net and a fish, we all leave with nothing
The net hauls in a thousand fish for the fisherman, who goes out of the world with empty hands
My uncle fished with a big net for fifty years and made decent money, but he died with nothing in his pockets and his sons sold the net and the fish he left the following week
net, fish, nothing carried
Write a doha in which a fisherman casts his net for fish all his life, piling up silver and fame, but who departs the world with nothing in his hands and no kin walking beside him
doha about leaving with nothing, make it short and simple
The rich man and the pauper are weighed at the end by the same quiet hand, and both are found to carry nothing
After the will was read the family hardly spoke; the man who built all this left with only the clothes on his body
Please write a doha that reminds a proud man that the wealth he hoards, the friends he flatters and the name he polishes will all be left behind when he steps onto the last road
nothing goes with us
doha with a blind man and cotton, you leave the world with nothing
Please write a doha about a blind man who sleeps on a bed of cotton and thinks himself rich, but who goes out of the world with nothing, like a king, carrying neither his bed nor his name
The blind man counts his cotton by touch, and the last journey counts his hands, which hold nothing
blind man, cotton, bare hands
The blind man who lived beside the cotton warehouse died poor, and the owner of the warehouse died rich, and the same plain cloth covered both; neither took anything
All the roads of earth lead to a gate where the guard accepts neither coin nor kin nor honour
Write a doha in which the rich and the poor arrive at the same gate at the end of life, both with open hands, because no wealth, no relatives and no fame can pass through
doha about nothing coming with us when we die
empty-handed, all of us
At the funeral they said, he came with nothing and he leaves with nothing, and I looked at the line of expensive cars outside; I want a doha for this feeling
net, lotus, nothing carried
doha with a net and a lotus, you cant take anything with you
Please write a doha in which a person casts a net over every pleasure and pulls in wealth like a lotus pond in bloom, but who walks out of the world with a bare hand and a bare heart
I watched my grandfather mend his net by the lotus pond on his last evening, and the next morning all his work was nobody's; he took not a knot
The net is full, the lotus open, and the hand that held them goes out as empty as it came
doha about a tortoise carrying its shell but we cant carry anything
tortoise, nothing goes along
The tortoise carries his shell wherever he goes, but man cannot carry so much as a coin into the dark
Write a doha about a tortoise who carries his home everywhere on his back, contrasting with human beings who build large houses and collect wealth yet must leave the world with nothing at all
We saw a tortoise carrying its whole shell across the road, and my father said if only we could carry our property like that; he died last year and took not one rupee
My cousin got a thorn in his foot at his father's funeral, and the bier passed with not a thing of his father's riches on it; we all stood bare-handed
The thorn pricks the walking foot and the bier carries the body, and neither can carry the master's treasure
thorn, bier, nothing carried
Please write a doha in which a thorn and a bier are the only companions on the final road, showing that wealth and relatives and fame must stay behind and nothing at all travels with the departed
doha with a thorn and a bier, how everyone leaves with nothing
bitter gourd, empty hands
doha with a bitter gourd, everyone leaves with nothing
My mother grew a bitter gourd vine that fed the whole lane, and she died owning nothing but that vine and a few pots, and she took none of it
The bitter gourd is shared with the neighbours, and the owner leaves the garden as she entered it, with empty hands
Write a doha in which the bitter gourd on the wall grows for whoever picks it, to show that nothing in this world truly belongs to anyone, and that every person leaves with empty hands
Kabir often sang that we arrive bare and leave bare, so please write a doha for me in simple words about how pointless it is to cling to wealth, family and fame when none of it goes with us
My grandmother gave away her last few things before she died and said she did not want to take any quarrel along; I loved her for it, and I want a doha about that
doha on leaving this world with nothing in hand
nothing at the end
The earth receives the body, and the heirs receive the keys, and the soul receives nothing, and asks for nothing
potter and clay, bee, nothing
doha with a potter and clay and a bee, about leaving with nothing
The potter and clay make the pot and the bee gathers honey, and neither can carry its labour out of the world
Our village potter and clay supplier made a thousand pots, and a bee built a hive in his kiln; when he died he left nothing but a stack of cracked ones
Please write a doha in which a potter and clay and a bee labour all their lives for something that will pass to others, to show that no one can carry his earnings out of this world
elephant, nothing goes along
doha about an elephant and how you cant take anything with you
The elephant in his golden ornaments goes down to the earth like the poorest, taking nothing but a trunk of dust

Write a doha about a king's elephant, heavy with ornaments and carrying banners, which is led out of the stable after the king's death, to show that none of the glory could accompany the master on his last road
The elephant at our village festival is decorated like a king, but my grandfather died owning less than its ankle bracelets, and he was just as peaceful; he took nothing
doha with a shroud and a pearl, you only take the shroud
shroud, pearl, nothing else
We dressed my father in a plain shroud and the pearl he treasured stayed in the box, because it could not go with him
Please write a doha about a man who owns a pearl but leaves the world wearing only a shroud, to show how little goes with the departed and how much is left behind for others
Wrapped in a shroud, the pearl-bearer departs, and not one pearl accompanies him through the dark
Write a doha about a traveler and a peacock, showing that the traveler arrives at the end of the road with nothing, though he walked proudly as a peacock on the way and gathered treasures
doha with a traveler and a peacock, how you leave with nothing
My uncle, a traveler, strutted like a peacock, buying gifts for everyone, and at the end of his road he stood in the doctor's waiting room with nothing but his ticket
traveler, peacock, nothing carried
The traveler struts like a peacock down the long road, and arrives at the end with nothing to show
empty hands
My brother and I fought for years over our father's land, and at his funeral I saw his open palms and could not remember what we were fighting for
doha on how we all leave with nothing in hand

Write a doha in Kabir's voice that reminds people their money, their children and their fame will stay on this side of the last road, and that they should be careful what they spend their lives pursuing
The great hand of the world takes back everything it lent, and returns the guest with nothing
The swan and the traveler come to the end of the same lake, and neither takes a drop of it along
doha with a swan and a traveler, you cant take anything with you
Please write a doha in which a swan and a traveler pause at the shore, the traveler has a bag of coins and the swan has nothing, and both must leave empty of everything when their road ends
A traveler passed through our village with a bag of coins and he died at the pond where the swan lives; the bag stayed on the bank
swan, traveler, nothing carried
He built the biggest hut in the village, planted a date palm in front of it to mark his name, and was carried out with nothing; the palm still stands

Please write a doha about a date palm planted by a proud man to mark his name, which outlasts him by many years while he himself left the world with empty hands and left his wealth to quarrelling heirs
doha with a date palm about leaving with nothing
The date palm stands tall for a hundred years, but no one has ever carried one of its dates to the other shore
date palm, nothing carried
doha about gold and how nobody takes it with them
My aunt kept her gold in a steel trunk under the bed all her life, and when she died, my cousins opened it before the funeral was even over; she took nothing
Gold shines in the dark of the chest, and the dark of the grave takes the owner without a speck
Write a doha in which a woman hides gold in a cellar, counts it each night, and dies with a bare hand while it lies untouched, showing that no wealth can cross the border of death
gold, nothing goes along
Write a doha in which a thorn pricks the foot of a rich man on the way to his last journey, and he realises that all he has gathered, his wealth, family and name, will stay behind
My uncle had a thorn in his foot for a month, which he blamed for his foul mood, but what hurt most at his funeral was that all his wealth stayed with us
thorn, nothing carried
The thorn is small and the treasure is great, yet both are left at the roadside when the walker goes
doha with a thorn about leaving everything behind when we die
Please write a doha about a bitter gourd that hangs on a wall for the neighbours to take, as a lesson to the man who thinks his wealth is his own but must leave the world with open hands
The bitter gourd hangs and is taken by the passerby, and so is the wealth of the proudest man
bitter gourd, nothing carried
doha with a bitter gourd, you cant take anything with you
The old widow's bitter gourd vine was picked clean by the neighbours the week after she died, and I thought of how everything we hold gets taken by someone else
My mother wore the same pearl earring for forty years, and when she died it was all she had; she took even that off before the end and gave it to me
doha with a pearl about how you leave without anything
The pearl is the sea's gift to a rich woman, and at the last she returns it to the world with her bare breath
pearl, nothing goes along
Write a doha about a pearl that is worn proudly by its owner until the final day, when it is removed from the body and stays behind, showing that not even the dearest object can go with the soul
The dawn finds the king in his court and the evening finds him with nothing, as the court stays and the king does not
doha on how nobody takes any of their wealth with them
My great-uncle owned three trucks and a mill, and when he passed the mill was shut by the next evening; he left with a single bead of tulsi round his neck
bare hands

Please write a doha in simple words, in the tone of Kabir, that explains how the powerful and the humble arrive with open hands and leave in the same way, taking nothing of their wealth and their relations
When my father died there was a long list of his accounts, but at the funeral the only thing he carried was the cloth he was wrapped in
The last journey has no baggage, and the one who comes with a hundred trunks is searched at the gate and sent in bare
doha on leaving with nothing, with a funeral feel
Write a doha reminding us that the mansion, the bank balance and the crowds at a wedding are all left on this side of the final road, and that only our deeds make the journey with us
empty hands
The sand runs through the fingers and the scales balance only the breath, and the rich man exits with the poor man's portion
doha with sand and scales, you leave everything behind when you die
My uncle weighed things on his scales at his shop all his life, and the day he died there was only a handful of sand on the floor where his stock used to be; he took nothing
sand, scales, nothing carried

Please write a doha in which a merchant uses scales to weigh everything he owns and watches sand slip through his fingers, while the verse says that nothing he weighed can be carried across when he dies
doha on leaving this world with nothing, keep it plain

Compose a Kabir-style doha that says the one who goes to the next world goes alone, with no treasure, no wife, no children and no fame at his side, and who therefore should not spend a lifetime collecting them
At my brother's funeral I noticed that nobody had brought anything for him; that is when it struck me how little a man really takes with him
nothing at the end
One by one the gifts, the faces and the names fall away at the doorway of the last day, and the soul walks in bare
doha with a crossroads, everyone leaves with nothing
At the crossroads of the last day, the rich and the poor are sent by the same road, and neither has anything to carry
crossroads, empty hands
Write a doha about a man who stands at a crossroads at the end of his life with a heavy bag of wealth, and learns that the road he must take admits no baggage at all
My grandfather died in a village crossroads accident carrying a bag of savings for his granddaughter's wedding; the bag was returned, but he went with nothing
The moon lights the washerman's riverbank where he washes the rich man's clothes, and the clothes outlast the owner who leaves bare
Please write a doha about a washerman who washes the fine clothes of a rich family under the moon, and who knows that when the rich man dies he will take none of those clothes with him
moon, washerman, nothing carried
The washerman in our street has washed every wedding sari under the moon for decades, and he says the one thing he never sees on a dead man is jewellery
doha with the moon and a washerman, nobody takes anything with them
Write a doha in which a thorn lies in the path of a man carrying a bag of coins on his last journey, and the thorn catches the bag and tears it away, so that he walks on with nothing
thorn, nothing goes along
doha with a thorn, you leave the world with nothing
There was a thorn bush by the road where my grandfather's body was carried, and it tugged at the cloth like it wanted to take something from him, but there was nothing
The thorn clutches at the departing man's sleeve, and finds there only a breath
